title: Grade 6 Science — Mon, Jun 01
description: Fibre to Fabric — Day 1 of 5: Natural fibres and their sources
subject: science

questions.question: The thin, thread-like strands from which fabrics are made are called:
questions.explanation: Fibres are thin thread-like strands that are spun into yarn and woven into fabric.

questions.question: Fibres obtained from plants and animals are called:
questions.explanation: Natural fibres come from plant or animal sources, like cotton, jute, wool and silk.

questions.question: Cotton fibre is obtained from the:
questions.explanation: Cotton is obtained from the fluffy fibres found in the cotton bolls (fruits) of the cotton plant.

questions.question: Jute fibre is obtained from the ____ of the jute plant.
questions.explanation: Jute is obtained from the stem of the jute plant.

questions.question: Wool is a natural fibre obtained from:
questions.explanation: Wool is an animal fibre obtained from sheep, goats and some other animals.

questions.question: Silk fibre is obtained from the:
questions.explanation: Silk is obtained from the cocoon spun by the silkworm.

questions.question: Which of these is a plant fibre?
questions.explanation: Cotton is a plant fibre; wool and silk are animal fibres and nylon is synthetic.

questions.question: Which two of these are animal fibres?
questions.explanation: Wool and silk are both obtained from animals, so they are animal fibres.

questions.question: Cotton plants grow best in places with:
questions.explanation: Cotton needs a warm climate and grows well in black soil.

questions.question: Jute is mainly grown in India during the:
questions.explanation: Jute is grown during the rainy season as it needs plenty of water.

questions.question: Fibres made from chemicals, not from plants or animals, are called:
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres, like nylon and polyester, are made from chemicals.

questions.question: Which of these is a synthetic fibre?
questions.explanation: Polyester is a synthetic (man-made) fibre, while cotton, jute and wool are natural.

questions.question: Long ago, before fabrics, people used ____ to cover their bodies.
options: Tree bark, leaves and animal skins
questions.explanation: Early humans used bark, large leaves and animal skins and furs before they learned to make fabric.

questions.question: Why is cotton clothing comfortable in summer?
options: It absorbs sweat and lets air pass
questions.explanation: Cotton absorbs sweat and allows air to pass, keeping us cool in summer.

questions.question: Group correctly: which list has only natural fibres?
questions.explanation: Cotton, wool and silk are all natural fibres from plants or animals.
